standard.title: Estimate likelihoods from frequency
standard.description: Conduct repeated chance experiments including those with and without equally likely outcomes, observe and record the results; use frequency to compare outcomes and estimate their likelihoods
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can list possible outcomes and compare equally and unequally likely experiments (AC9M5P01). They have not yet used experimental frequency to estimate probability or compared experimental to theoretical likelihood.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students conduct repeated chance experiments, record results, and use frequency to compare outcomes and estimate likelihoods.

nodes.label: Conducting and recording experiments
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can conduct a chance experiment with repeated trials and record results systematically.
nodes.minimum_width: Conduct a chance experiment with at least 20 trials; record results in a tally or frequency table.
nodes.typical_width: Conduct experiments with and without equally likely outcomes; record in organised frequency tables; use digital tools to simulate large numbers of trials.
wider: Combine class data to increase trial count and compare results
Design a recording system that tracks running totals as well as individual results
success_criteria: Student conducts a chance experiment with systematic recording
Student produces a complete, accurate frequency table for the experiment

nodes.label: Using frequency to estimate likelihood
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use relative frequency from experiments to estimate the likelihood of outcomes and compare outcomes.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate the relative frequency of each outcome from experimental data; use this to rank outcomes from most to least likely.
nodes.typical_width: Calculate relative frequencies as fractions and percentages; compare relative frequencies across experimental conditions (equal vs unequal likelihood); use frequency estimates to make predictions.
wider: Compare experimental frequency estimates from small vs large trial counts
Use digital simulations to explore how relative frequency stabilises with more trials

response_modes.reason: The relationship between sample size and reliability of frequency estimates is not obvious. Multiple contexts with different trial counts help students develop intuition about when experimental estimates are trustworthy.
Using frequency to estimate likelihood requires conducting experiments, organising data and applying fraction/percentage reasoning together — these must coordinate for the estimate to be meaningful.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Digital simulation investigation of the Law of Large Numbers is genuinely rich for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student calculates relative frequency correctly from experimental data
Student uses relative frequency to rank or compare outcomes

nodes.label: Comparing experimental and theoretical likelihood
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compare experimental relative frequencies to expected theoretical likelihoods and discuss reasons for differences.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare experimental relative frequencies for an equally likely experiment to the theoretical probability; describe similarities and differences.
nodes.typical_width: Conduct experiments, calculate relative frequencies, and compare to theoretical probabilities for equally and unequally likely experiments; discuss how sample size affects agreement.
wider: Investigate how the Law of Large Numbers causes experimental and theoretical values to converge
Design an experiment to determine whether an unknown spinner is fair using relative frequency evidence

response_modes.reason: Comparing experimental and theoretical probability requires conducting experiments, calculating relative frequencies, applying fraction/percentage reasoning and interpreting theoretical probability — these all coordinate at this node.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Fair/unfair spinner investigation using evidence is genuinely rich for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student correctly compares experimental relative frequency to theoretical probability
Student discusses at least one reason the values may differ
